about: I’m Jerikho Raphael Stefian, a Computer Science student at BINUS University in Indonesia, specializing in Artificial Intelligence.
I enjoy taking things apart conceptually: understanding how a model makes a prediction, what a security event reveals, or how a tool can make everyday work easier.
Beyond the screen, I like traveling, exploring new places, and learning about financial markets. Mentoring and volunteering remind me that good technical work starts with understanding people.

projects.title: Automatic Meeting Summarizer
projects.summary: Turning meeting transcripts into concise summaries with a fine-tuned language model.
projects.intro: A web application that turns written meeting transcripts into summaries using a fine-tuned PEGASUS model.
projects.heading: How it works
points: Accepts a written transcript through a browser interface.
Cleans whitespace, tokenizes the input, and generates a summary using PEGASUS.
Connects the model to a Flask API for browser-based interaction.
projects.note: This application processes text transcripts. The current inference code truncates inputs to 512 tokens; it does not transcribe audio.

projects.title: House Price Prediction
projects.summary: Connecting a machine learning model to an interactive property price estimator.
projects.intro: An Ames Housing price prediction project connecting an XGBoost regression model to a Streamlit interface.
projects.heading: From features to an estimate
points: Uses a trained XGBoost model to estimate a property’s sale price.
Accepts six features: total floor area, lot area, year built, bedrooms, bathrooms, and garage capacity.
Provides an interactive interface for entering property details and viewing model predictions.
projects.note: Predictions are model estimates for a learning project, not property valuations. The portfolio chart is illustrative and does not represent evaluation results.

projects.title: Mini SOC Lab
projects.summary: Exploring endpoint telemetry, Windows event logs, and security alert investigation.
projects.intro: A hands-on lab for understanding how Windows endpoint telemetry becomes evidence during a security investigation.
projects.heading: What I practiced
points: Configured a Wazuh-based environment to collect and analyze endpoint security events.
Explored Windows authentication logs and relevant event fields to understand login activity.
Reviewed alerts and event data to practice security event triage and investigation workflows.
projects.note: This is a personal lab project. It demonstrates foundational monitoring and investigation practice, rather than production SOC experience.

projects.title: Malware Image Classification
projects.summary: Exploring image-based representations for machine learning malware classification.
projects.intro: A machine learning project exploring malware classification through image-based representations.
projects.heading: The idea
points: Represent malware samples as images for a classification task.
Explore how visual patterns can support machine learning classification.
Connect interests in artificial intelligence and security analysis.
projects.note: Explore the implementation and project materials in the repository.

projects.title: SplitEase
projects.summary: An Android app for splitting bills with receipt recognition and shared sessions.
projects.intro: An Android application designed to make shared expense management easier through receipt recognition and shareable expense sessions.
projects.heading: What the application does
points: Manages shared bills and calculates individual payment amounts.
Uses Google Cloud Vision OCR to extract receipt text.
Uses Firebase Realtime Database to share expense sessions through links.
projects.note: Developed February–June 2026, with hands-on experience integrating external APIs and cloud services.
